text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Slovenian newspapers.
- The foreign ministry said it has not yet been officially informed that the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia wanted to normalise its relations with Slovenia.
- The parliament said a new law on doctors should not lead to a significant rise in doctors' salaries. It said doctors should be included in a general law covering the whole of the public sector.
- The Chamber of Economy has said it insists that a general collective agreement determining workers' benefits be changed from January 1997.
- The Ljubelj border tunnel between Slovenia and Austria was opened on Thursday after being closed for over a month after part of construction collapsed on the Slovenian side.
- The parliament has not yet passed a bill on police forces that was prepared about two years ago. The current law on police dates back to 1980.
- A delegation of the European Parliament will end its three-day visit to Slovenia on Friday.
- The Slovenian Association of Managers named the chief executive of the food company Kolinska Lojze Dezelak as the manager of the year.

- Most companies in Slovenia, that are fully or partially in foreign ownership, claim they have managed to balance workforce expenses by increasing work efficiency and have therefore no plans to cut work benefits.
- Fresh capital of foreign and domestic investors has been pushing prices on the Ljubljana bourse up for the past three weeks.
